sections.html:
Listing with an agent, selling without one and taking a cash buyer's as-is bid are all open to a Waukegan owner. The city paperwork is the same for all three, so the choice mostly turns on how much repair work, waiting and showing you want to take on.

Waukegan faces Lake Michigan, roughly 11 miles below the Wisconsin line and 37 miles up the shore from downtown Chicago, and no other Lake County city has more people. The 2020 census counted 89,321, and the mid-2025 estimate is 87,940. The city has about 32,000 households, and it adds a transfer step that many Illinois towns do not have, covered next.

Every change of ownership in Waukegan needs a zoning certificate, a life-safety inspection and a closing letter, under Ordinance 23-0-294. The city's Closing Letter / Zoning Certificate page has the application.

File the online application when you list, and in any case at least 30 days ahead of closing. A code officer calls within five days of the fee payment to book a minimal code and life-safety inspection. The certificate has to hang where it is fully visible, as near the front entrance as possible, for the whole time the home is on the market.

The ordinance has no exceptions, so foreclosure and tax-sale transfers need the same documents. Each parcel number in a sale needs its own closing letter, and a missing number can hold up the closing.

  • Seller side: property details, occupancy status, number of bedrooms or units, MLS number if listed, and the listing agent's contact information.
  • Buyer side, once you have one: a driver's license number for the water account transfer, receipts for any city amounts already settled, and a notarized affidavit.
  • Utility side: call the Water Department at least five business days before closing to schedule the final meter reading (847-360-0535).

sections.h2: Costs and steps of a Waukegan sale
sections.html:
These city and county items attach to a house sale.

Waukegan and Lake County items attached to a house sale
Cost or stepAmount or rule
Zoning certificate application fee$150.00, due when you submit
Closing letter application fee$150.00, for a $300 total at submittal
TimingApply at listing, at least 30 days before closing
Final water readingSchedule at least five business days before closing
Recording a standard deed$70 flat fee, plus any transfer tax due
Recording a non-standard document$82 flat fee

The closing letter is issued only after the fees and the final water bill are paid. Any liens on the property are disclosed in the record, and the payoff statements can be settled at closing.

Yes, with conditions. The city allows an as-is sale when the zoning certificate inspection is done and the buyer signs a notarized affidavit. The city provides no template, so the affidavit has to carry a date, the buyer's address, phone number and email, a list of the items the buyer takes on from the inspection report, the buyer's signature and the notary's confirmation.

A cash buyer who agrees to take the inspection items does not hold the closing up for repairs, though the inspection itself still has to happen. Sellers who wait until a contract is signed to apply risk running into the 30-day window.

State law adds a separate duty: residential sellers give the buyer a completed disclosure report before signing (765 ILCS 77/20). Transfers from an estate fiduciary, by court order or in lieu of foreclosure are among the exempt ones listed in Section 15.

Owners and renters split the city almost evenly: owners occupy 50.2% of homes. The middle value of an owned home is $190,900, well under suburbs to the south, and the middle rent with utilities is $1,205 a month. The city has 32,042 households of about 2.72 people, with a midpoint household income of $71,919.

The city has also pursued a lakefront plan to replace much of the old industrial shoreline with residential and recreational space. Most of Waukegan belongs to Waukegan Community Unit School District 60, but pieces fall inside Gurnee School District 56 and a small section sits in Beach Park District 3 and Zion-Benton District 126, so check the district named on your tax bill before describing schools in a listing. Commuters look at the Metra Union Pacific North line, the Tri-State Tollway and the Amstutz Expressway.

The city's rental license page explains that every rental inside city limits needs a license before anyone moves in. Licenses expire each December 31, the fee is $60 per rented unit, and an application needs planning and zoning pre-approval plus a passed inspection by the Building and Code Department. A code officer reaches out within five business days to schedule it.

Where tenants occupy the house, keep the license current while it is listed and tell prospective buyers about the lease early. Ask the city's License Department how the license is handled when ownership changes.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Lake County
sections.html:
Deeds for Waukegan homes are filed in the county building at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office (phone 847-377-2575). Its fee schedule lists a $70 standard document fee and an $82 non-standard fee, and the only other charges at recording are state and county transfer taxes.

The county's deed packet lists what must be on the document.

  • Signed and dated by the grantor, with a notary acknowledgment
  • The buyer's address, a full legal description and the preparer's name and address
  • A "mail to" address and the name and address for tax bills
  • A completed PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement

The state tax follows 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which prints the rate as 50¢ per $500 of the value stated in the declaration, counting any fraction of $500. The same packet names six Lake County municipalities that require a local stamp before recording. Waukegan is not on that list, though the closing letter described above applies.

sections.h2: A cash sale from start to finish
sections.html:
Start the city application the day the house is under agreement, or sooner. While the inspector's visit and the closing letter move along, the title company searches the record, and you gather payoff statements for any mortgage or lien.

Before closing day, call the Water Department for the final meter reading and pay the last bill. At the table you sign the deed, the buyer signs the affidavit if the sale is as-is, and the deed goes to the Lake County Clerk for recording. With no lender involved, the city steps and the title work are the whole schedule.

faqs.q: Must a Waukegan seller repair every item the inspector lists?
faqs.a: No. The city allows an as-is sale if the buyer signs a notarized affidavit accepting the listed items. The inspection still has to be done and the certificate issued, so apply as soon as the house is listed or under agreement.

faqs.q: What does the Waukegan closing letter process cost?
faqs.a: The city lists $300 at submittal, split into a $150 zoning certificate fee and a $150 closing letter fee. Any other invoiced amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are settled before the letter is issued.

faqs.q: Do foreclosure and tax-sale transfers in Waukegan skip the certificate?
faqs.a: No. The city's ordinance lists no exemptions for transfers such as foreclosure or tax sale, so those transfers also need the application, inspection and closing letter.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Waukegan closing?
faqs.a: The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office takes it, at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Bring it in or send it by mail; the office phone is 847-377-2575.

faqs.q: How soon can a Waukegan cash sale close?
faqs.a: The city's steps set the minimum: apply at listing, at least 30 days before closing, with an inspector calling within five business days. An as-is buyer can follow that schedule, and title work sets the rest.
